script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for April 6. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Before numbers, humans could only vaguely compare quantities.  'More' or 'less. ' 'Many' or 'few.

Humans have an innate sense of quantity—we can instantly distinguish 3 from 4 items. But this 'number sense' only works for small amounts. For larger quantities, we needed numbers—symbols that extend our natural limits. Zero was invented surprisingly late—around 500 CE in India.  The idea that 'nothing' could be 'something'—a number you could calculate with—was philosophically radical.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Abstraction is power.  Numbers show that representing things with symbols lets us think thoughts that would otherwise be impossible.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Number Awareness - See the Invisible System.

Here's your activity: Today, notice every time you use numbers: checking time, spending money, measuring, counting. Numbers are so embedded in modern life that we forget they're a technology—one that makes complex civilization possible. This helps you appreciate numbers as a powerful cognitive tool.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why numbers were invented can be applied to number awareness - see the invisible system. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
